note: AI-written (Claude, Anthropic) for the team's NASA Space Apps 2026 project. Shot list for the Marswalk tour video. 'say' is the narration (one audio file per segment, audio/<id>.mp3). 'bubble' is the short text in the speech bubble. 'point' and 'do' are plain words; film.mjs maps them to selectors and actions.

segments.say: Hi, I'm Claude. This is Marswalk, the app I built with the team for NASA Space Apps. It plans one astronaut walk on Mars and then replays it. Let me show you how it works.
segments.bubble: Marswalk: plan one walk on Mars, then replay it
segments.point: the product name plate, top left
segments.do: Open the app with no URL option. Step 1 shows and the scene turns slowly. Do nothing else.

segments.say: This is the place: the boxwork ridges on Mount Sharp, in Gale crater. The ground shape is real terrain data at one metre. The picture on top is a real orbit image at 25 centimetres. Both come from USGS and NASA files.
segments.bubble: Real terrain at 1 m, real orbit image at 25 cm
segments.point: the caption plate, bottom left (headline and text)
segments.do: Keep the scene turning. Move the cursor slowly from the name plate to the caption plate.

segments.say: The app is a story in five steps: Place, Plan, Walk, Hazard and Check. One thing per screen, and one big button to go on.
segments.bubble: Five steps. One big Next button.
segments.point: first the stepper, top centre; then the Next button 'See the plan'
segments.do: Move the cursor along the five step buttons without a click, then down to the Next button. Do not click yet.

segments.say: You can move the map yourself. Drag to move, scroll to zoom. Or use these buttons: zoom, tilt, turn, north up, and fit.
segments.bubble: Drag, scroll, or use these buttons
segments.point: the map control cluster, bottom right
segments.do: Click zoom in twice, turn right three times, then drag the map a short way with the mouse. End with a click on the last button (fit).

segments.say: Step two is the plan. The magenta line is the route. It starts and ends at the crew rover, the base, and it visits eight science stations.
segments.bubble: Magenta = the route, from the base through 8 stations
segments.point: the BASE tag first, then the route line near station S1
segments.do: Click the Next button 'See the plan'. Wait until the route shows. Move the cursor from the BASE tag down along the route to S1.

segments.say: A filled square is a station on a ridge. An open square is a station in a hollow. The hatched areas are no-go zones. The planner keeps the route out of them, and it keeps every leg at or under a slope of 15 degrees.
segments.bubble: Filled = ridge. Open = hollow. Hatch = no-go.
segments.point: a ridge station tag (S1), then a hollow station tag (S2), then a no-go zone hatch
segments.do: Move the cursor to S1, then S2, then to the hatched no-go zone near S3.

segments.say: Here are the four numbers that matter: the distance, the time in the suit, the steepest slope against its limit, and how many limits the plan keeps.
segments.bubble: The four numbers of the walk
segments.point: the key numbers grid in the caption plate
segments.do: Move the cursor over the four key numbers, one after the other.

segments.say: Click a station and its card opens. It says where the station is, and the one task that a person does there and a rover could not do in the same time.
segments.bubble: Click a station for its task
segments.point: the station tag S6, then the station card that opens
segments.do: Click station tag S6. Keep the card open while the audio runs. Then close the card with its Close button.

segments.say: These switches add data on top of the map. Slope shows where the ground is steep. Rover path shows where Curiosity drove. Height shows the terrain height.
segments.bubble: Quick layers: Slope, Rover path, Height
segments.point: the three layer chips in the caption plate
segments.do: Click chip Slope, wait 2 s, click Slope off. Click Rover path, wait 2 s, click it off. Click Height, wait 2 s, click it off.

segments.say: Every number in the app knows where it comes from. Turn on Show sources, and each number tells you: a named source, a value we derived from the terrain, or an assumption.
segments.bubble: Show sources: each number says where it comes from
segments.point: the 'Show sources' switch, top right; then the labels under the key numbers
segments.do: Click the Show sources switch (on). Move the cursor to the key numbers. At the end of the audio click the switch again (off).

segments.say: Everything else is behind one button: Details. The first tab holds the limits of the walk, each with its source and its margin.
segments.bubble: Details: all panels in one place
segments.point: the Details button, then the Limits table in the drawer
segments.do: Click Details. The drawer opens on the Limits tab. Move the cursor down the limits table.

segments.say: The other tabs: the timeline with the height profile. All data layers, with the conditions that Curiosity measured. The stations. An editor, where the team can change stations, no-go zones and assumed values, and the app plans again. And the credits, with every source and its licence.
segments.bubble: Timeline, Layers, Stations, Editor, Credits
segments.point: each drawer tab in turn
segments.do: Click the tabs in this order, about equal time each: Timeline, Layers, Stations, Editor, Credits. Scroll each panel a little if it is longer than the drawer. At the end close the drawer.

segments.say: Step three is the walk. Now we are at eye height, and the walk replays. This is the helmet display. It is a simulation, and it says so.
segments.bubble: Eye height. The helmet display.
segments.point: the SIMULATION label, top left
segments.do: Click the Next button 'Start the walk'. The view drops to eye height and plays at 60x. Move the cursor to the SIMULATION label.

segments.say: At the top: the next station, with its bearing and distance. On the right: three margins. Suit time left, range to the rover, and range to the partner. You see how much is left before a limit.
segments.bubble: Next station. Three margins.
segments.point: the top centre block (next station, bearing, distance), then the margins block top right
segments.do: Let the walk play. Move the cursor to the bearing and distance, then to the three margins.

segments.say: At the bottom left is the science line. This ground temperature is a value that Curiosity measured in this area, on sol 4600. The small map shows where you are. And the camera turns like a person who looks ahead.
segments.bubble: Measured by Curiosity, sol 4600
segments.point: the science line bottom left, then the map inset bottom right
segments.do: Let the walk play. Move the cursor to the science line, then to the map inset.

segments.say: A suited astronaut has only three actions, each a large button and a key: Next, Acknowledge, and Return to rover. Down here you can pause and change the speed.
segments.bubble: Three actions. Pause and speed below.
segments.point: the three helmet action buttons, then the walk bar (Pause, speed)
segments.do: Move the cursor over Return to rover, Acknowledge, Next (no click). Then click Pause, click Play, click speed 240x.

segments.say: When you arrive at a station, its card opens with the task, and the work time runs.
segments.bubble: Arrival: the station card
segments.point: the station card on the helmet display, bottom left
segments.do: Before the audio starts, use the helmet Next action (key N) until the walker is at a station in work mode with the card open, then set speed 60x. Point at the card.

segments.say: Step four is a hazard. A solar particle event that was recorded near Earth in May 2025 is replayed here as a scenario. We do not claim that it arrived at Mars.
segments.bubble: Scenario: a recorded solar particle event
segments.point: the scenario sentence in the walk bar
segments.do: Click the Next button 'Go to the hazard'. Wait until RETURN NOW shows. Point at the scenario sentence in the walk bar.

segments.say: The display says: return now. A shape and a word, so the warning does not depend on colour. It gives the bearing and the distance back to the rover and the walk-back time. The red line is the way back.
segments.bubble: RETURN NOW, with the way back
segments.point: the RETURN NOW box, then the bearing and distance to the base, then the red path on the map inset
segments.do: Point at RETURN NOW, then at the bearing and distance, then at the map inset. Click Play so the walker starts the way back for a few seconds. At the end click Acknowledge.

segments.say: The last step checks our map against the real rover. The blue line is where Curiosity drove in 2025. Ninety-two percent of its positions are under the slope cap on our map, and our slope differs from the tilt that the rover measured by 2.8 degrees in the median.
segments.bubble: Blue = where Curiosity really drove
segments.point: the blue Curiosity path, then the three key numbers
segments.do: Click the Next button 'See the rover check'. Move the cursor along the blue path, then over the key numbers.

segments.say: If the display fails, there is a route card for print. One page: each leg with its bearing, distance, climb and time, and the task at each station.
segments.bubble: The route card: one printed page
segments.point: the button 'Print the route card', then the sheet that opens
segments.do: Click 'Print the route card'. The sheet opens (do not start the browser print dialog). Scroll the sheet slowly down and up. Close the sheet at the end.

segments.say: After the story you can explore on your own. And if a device cannot draw 3D, the app loads a flat map from the same files.
segments.bubble: Explore freely
segments.point: the button 'Explore freely'
segments.do: Click 'Explore freely'. The drawer opens and leg labels show. Zoom in once and drag the map a little.

segments.say: That is Marswalk. One walk, real data, and every number with its origin. Some values are assumptions, like the walking speed, and the app labels them. Thanks for watching.
segments.bubble: One walk. Real data. Every number with its origin.
segments.point: nothing (hide the pointer)
segments.do: Close the drawer, click 'Back to the story', go to step 1 with the stepper so the turning scene is the last picture.
